new_events.summary: Reuters-verified video showed armored vehicles from Yemeni government forces striking and running over Houthi fighters near Bab el-Mandeb, including unarmed men. The Giants Brigade said it opened an investigation. The Houthis called the footage evidence of war crimes. The reporting establishes the footage and investigation, not a legal adjudication.

Vice President JD Vance told Reuters that any agreement ending the war would require Iran to make a meaningful reduction in enrichment capacity. He said Washington was negotiating with President Masoud Pezeshkian, Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi and other political officials, while remaining uncertain how much decision authority they held inside Iran.

Yemen's Transport Ministry said the Houthis attacked Aden International Airport with ballistic missiles and explosive-laden drones. One missile landed near the runway shortly before a Cairo flight was due to land, forcing a diversion to Jeddah. The Saudi-led coalition separately reported intercepting Houthi ballistic missiles north of Riyadh and toward Khamis Mushait.

existing_event_updates.summary: Vance said Washington was negotiating with Pezeshkian, Araqchi and other political officials, but questioned how decisions were made inside Iran. He said meaningful enrichment reduction was required for an agreement ending the war. No agreement was announced.
Government forces continued consolidating around Bab el-Mandeb while Houthis struck Aden airport and Saudi Arabia reported intercepting missiles toward Riyadh and Khamis Mushait.

economic_energy_updates.summary: Brent settled October 6 at $100.58 per barrel and WTI at $89.44. The close preserved a risk premium despite strong Middle Eastern export recovery, reflecting continuing Saudi-Houthi escalation and other supply risks.
